text: Adapting large language models under strict hardware constraints requires navigating tradeoffs among parameter footprint, optimizer states, gradient graphs, and activation memory.

This research note synthesizes core methodologies for memory-efficient fine-tuning, analyzing low-rank parameterization (LoRA, AdaLoRA), structural frameworks, 8-bit optimizer compression, 4-bit base model quantization (QLoRA), and weight decomposition (DoRA).
We separate mathematical formulations from physical hardware measurements, present a structured comparison table, and outline a controlled single-GPU experimental protocol.

section: Memory Bottlenecks and Parameter-Efficient Adaptation Mechanics
text: Fine-tuning modern language models requires substantial high-bandwidth GPU memory (VRAM).

section: Memory Bottlenecks and Parameter-Efficient Adaptation Mechanics
text: During standard 16-bit mixed-precision training with 32-bit Adam, VRAM is dominated by four components: static weights (2 bytes per parameter), gradients (2 bytes), master weights and moment statistics (12 bytes per parameter), and dynamic forward activation buffers.

section: Memory Bottlenecks and Parameter-Efficient Adaptation Mechanics
text: For multi-billion parameter architectures, these 16 bytes per parameter quickly exceed single-GPU capacity before activations are allocated.

section: Memory Bottlenecks and Parameter-Efficient Adaptation Mechanics
text: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) addresses this bottleneck by freezing pre-trained model weights and updating only auxiliary parameters.

section: Memory Bottlenecks and Parameter-Efficient Adaptation Mechanics
text: LoRA freezes the pre-trained model weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices into each layer of the Transformer architecture.

section: Memory Bottlenecks and Parameter-Efficient Adaptation Mechanics
text: Because the vast majority of parameters remain frozen, gradient buffers and optimizer states are restricted to the low-rank matrices.

section: Memory Bottlenecks and Parameter-Efficient Adaptation Mechanics
text: LoRA reduces VRAM usage by up to 2/3 for a large Transformer trained with Adam by removing optimizer states for frozen parameters.

section: Quantization, Directional Decomposition, and Practical Tradeoffs
text: Even with frozen base parameters, 16-bit storage demands substantial VRAM (by our analytical estimate, ≈ 14 GB for a 7B model), requiring compression of optimizer states or base weights.

section: Quantization, Directional Decomposition, and Practical Tradeoffs
text: Block-wise dynamic quantization enables 8-bit optimizers that maintain 32-bit performance at a fraction of the original memory footprint.

section: Quantization, Directional Decomposition, and Practical Tradeoffs
text: Isolating tensors into 2048-element blocks enables 8-bit dynamic quantization of moments, reducing optimizer memory by three-quarters while maintaining numerical stability.

section: Quantization, Directional Decomposition, and Practical Tradeoffs
text: To reduce base weight memory, QLoRA pairs 4-bit base model quantization with 16-bit low-rank adapters.

section: Quantization, Directional Decomposition, and Practical Tradeoffs
text: QLoRA backpropagates gradients through a frozen 4-bit quantized pretrained language model into Low Rank Adapters.

section: Quantization, Directional Decomposition, and Practical Tradeoffs
text: QLoRA introduces 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4), double quantization, and paged optimizers.

section: Quantization, Directional Decomposition, and Practical Tradeoffs
text: Double Quantization quantizes the quantization constants, saving an average of about 0.37 bits per parameter.

section: Quantization, Directional Decomposition, and Practical Tradeoffs
text: Paged Optimizers use NVIDIA unified memory to avoid memory spikes during gradient checkpointing.

section: Quantization, Directional Decomposition, and Practical Tradeoffs
text: QLoRA reduces memory usage enough to finetune a 65B parameter model on a single 48GB GPU while preserving full 16-bit finetuning task performance.

section: Proposed Empirical Investigation on a Constrained GPU

text: However, key empirical limitations remain.

section: Limitations and Scope of Evidence
text: First, the reported memory reductions and performance parity from published benchmarks may not transfer directly to other model scales, sequence lengths, or consumer hardware environments without empirical measurement.

section: Limitations and Scope of Evidence
text: For example, fitting a 65B model into 48 GB does not guarantee proportional memory behavior for an 8B model on a 24 GB card where activation memory forms a larger fraction of total VRAM.

section: Limitations and Scope of Evidence
text: Second, the anecdotal laboratory pilot claiming a fifty percent memory reduction over LoRA lacks recorded experimental logs, hardware details, and baseline configurations, rendering it an unverified assertion.

section: Limitations and Scope of Evidence
text: Reliable adaptation research requires rigorous measurement rather than anecdotal claims.
